al.d: The Adams Farm at Penn’s Hill (John Adams and John Quincy Adams Birthplaces) is closed due to a major landscape treatment project. During construction, the entire site will be inaccessible. The Visitor Center and Peace field remain open and accessible.

al.t: Group Reservations
al.d: Groups of 11 or more people should contact the Visitor Center at ADAM_Visitor_Center@nps.gov or 617-770-1175 at least two weeks in advance to arrange their visit.

parks.te: Reservations for guided tours required. Reservations are required for guided tours. Self-guided tours do not require reservations. Access into the historic homes requires an entrance pass (fee). Access to the park grounds is free and does not require reservations or timed entry.

al.t: Archives and Collections Unavailable
al.d: The Agate Fossil Beds National Monument archive and collections are temporarily unavailable for research or study. If you have a pending research request or have questions, please send an email to scbl_afgo_superintendent@nps.gov and the park will contact you.

al.t: No Fuel Services
al.d: Fuel up before visiting! Agate Fossil Beds National Monument is 30-50 miles from the nearest service stations.

al.t: Limited Cell Phone Coverage
al.d: Cell phone voice and data coverage is very limited in the park and surrounding area. Free visitor WiFi is available in the visitor center.

al.t: Alcatraz Island Temporarily Closed for Dock Repairs October 26-November 18
al.d: Alcatraz Island, part of the Golden Gate National Recreation Area, is temporarily closed while crews replace pilings that secure the ferry dock to the island. Repairs are expected to be completed by November 18, 2026. For more information, please see news release linked here.

al.t: Auto-Theft Warning - Only Bring What You Need to the Park
al.d: You can help prevent vehicle break-ins in parking lots. Before leaving your car to catch the ferry: 1) Remove all valuables, 2) Lock your doors. 3) Take your wallets, purses, backpacks, keys, key fobs, cell phones, and electronics with you. Read article for more details.

al.t: Hospital wing, dining hall, shower room closed for rehabilitation work
al.d: Until approximately 2028, a portion of the cell house will be closed to visitors for important historic preservation work. We apologize for any inconvenience. Learn more at https://www.nps.gov/alca/alcatraz-historic-preservation-projects.htm

al.t: Staple Bend Tunnel Closure
al.d: Due to a rockfall, the interior of the Staple Bend Tunnel is closed. The trail is still open. From the Mineral Point Trailhead, visitors can bypass the tunnel, via a path around the right side of the tunnel structure.

al.t: No Visitor Center
al.d: Currently, there is no visitor center for Amache National Historic Site. There is a museum in the town of Granada that is operated by Amache Preservation Society. Learn more at amache.org

al.t: Limited Cell Phone Coverage
al.d: Cell phone voice and data coverage is very limited in the park and surrounding area.

al.t: Please use caution when visiting park grounds.
al.d: Park grounds and walking paths are accessible but visitors should use caution as there are fallen trees, stumps, and other typhoon debris.

al.t: Upcoming Hunt Area 2 Closures
al.d: Hunt Area 2 will be closed several dates due to law enforcement firearms qualifications. It will close at sundown, November 29th, and reopen sunrise, December 2nd. It will also close sundown, December 10th, and will reopen on sunrise, December 12.

al.t: Only Left Side of Rough Canyon, Box Canyon, and DE Boat Ramps Are Open
al.d: Due to low water levels, only the left side Rough Canyon, Box Canyon, and Diablo East boat ramps are open. The rest are closed. Please use caution with Spur 406 and Spur 454 launches, as the water may be too shallow to launch most boats. To see a list of open ramps, click on "more."

al.t: Diablo East Marina Cove, Scuba Cove, and Walkway Access Are Closed
al.d: The Diablo East Marina Cove, Scuba Cove, and walkway access are closed because of the presence of excessive docking material, unsafe walkway and dock, and unstable, loose ground. The area will reopen once these hazards have been corrected.

al.t: Help Prevent Aquatic Invasive Species (AIS) Infestation
al.d: A number of lakes are infested with an array of aquatic invasive species that damage natural ecosystems and waterways. Boaters are advised to Clean, Drain, and Dry all boats and equipment every time they leave the water.

al.t: Notice to travelers to National Cemetery
al.d: Due to the narrow roadway & tight turn, RVs, mobile homes, charter buses, delivery trucks, or vehicles with trailers are prohibited from the crest of Monument Hill. Check for information about parking at the Visitor Center upon your arrival.

al.t: Historic Andrew Johnson Homestead Reopens
al.d: The Home of our 17th president has reopened to the public. Daily tours available. See GUIDED TOURS information on website for more details.

al.t: Sherrick Farm Trail Detour
al.d: There is a detour on the trail due to downed trees. Our staff is working diligently to remove these from the trail.

al.t: Hunting Season Safety
al.d: Hunting is allowed in parts of Apostle Islands National Lakeshore from mid-September through early January. Wear blaze orange to stay visible and keep pets leashed and in bright vests. Make noise while hiking so others can hear you. Stay aware and enjoy a safe visit. Click the link below for more in

al.t: Bear Alert
al.d: Black bears inhabit many of the Apostle Islands. Follow safety guidelines: store food and scented items properly, hike in groups, stay attentive, and make noises if you encounter a bear in a visitor area.

al.t: Stockton Island Trail Access
al.d: The trail between Presque Isle Bay and Quarry Bay on Stockton Island is open, but a footbridge on the western portion of the trail was washed out in a 2024 storm. Visitors must wade through shallow water or take an alternate route.

al.t: Ongoing Closure Notices
al.d: Devils Island dock and campsites and West Bay Club on Sand Island are closed. These closures affect only a small portion of the Lakeshore. Enjoy your visit.

al.t: Private Inholdings: Sand & Rocky Islands
al.d: There are privately occupied residences and docks on the southeast corner of Sand Island, as well as just north of Group Site A on Rocky Island. These areas are closed to the public. Please respect their privacy and do not trespass in these locations.

al.t: List of trail closures post-Hurricane Helene
al.d: Many closures remain on the Trail following Hurricane Helene's devastation. This will remain true for the foreseeable future. Visit the Appalachian Trail Conservancy (ATC) website for an up-to-date list of closures. OBSERVE ALL CLOSURES. Stay safe!

al.t: Black Bears Frequenting the McAfee Knob Area in Virginia
al.d: Human-habituated bears have been frequently spotted in the McAfee Knob Area. Allowing bears access to human food or garbage causes it to lose its fear of humans. Follow all food storage regulations, use provided food lockers and never feed a bear.

al.d: Do not rely on GPS digital navigation systems to find your way to Badlands National Park. Please note that the Visitor Center at 25216 Ben Reifel Road, Interior SD 57750 is located just off I-90.

al.t: The Use of GPS is NOT Recommended
al.d: Numerous visitors have been routed to remote trailheads and out-of-the-way roads trying to use GPS to reach the main park area or shuttle stop.

al.t: Uber, Lyft, and Other "Taxi" Services
al.d: Bandelier is in a remote location, with cell service in the canyon limited to Verizon 4G only. Services like Uber and Lyft will bring you here, but there may be no way to contact a ride out. Please plan your pickup before being dropped off at Bandelier.

al.t: Plaza Access to Reconstructed Fort
al.d: Entry into the reconstructed fort is limited to the central plaza on scheduled days. For your safety respect all closures and restrictions. Guided tours provide access into additional areas.

al.t: Guided Tours at the Reconstructed Fort
al.d: Regularly scheduled guided tours provide access into furnished rooms and explore the fort’s role in Westward Expansion and the reconstruction of the fort in 1976.

al.t: A Short Walk is Required to Reach the Fort
al.d: A 1/4 mile (1,275 feet) walk on a paved trail from the parking area is required to reach the gate of the fort. At the end of your visit, you'll return to your vehicle along the same path.

al.d: The windsock at the Serpentine Hot Springs airstrip is broken, and the National Park Service is in the process of ordering a replacement. At this time, we do not have an estimated date for when it will be reinstalled. Please use caution when utilizing the airstrip.

al.d: Our phone lines are working intermittently. If you are not able to reach us by phone, please email us at bela_information@nps.gov.

al.t: Big Bend is a NO DRONE Zone
al.d: The use of drones is prohibited in Big Bend National Park. Thank you for preserving the peace and tranquility of Big Bend.

al.t: Bringing a Pet to Big Bend?

al.t: Black Bears at Big South Fork
al.d: Black bears call Big South Fork NRRA home. Help keep them healthy and safe by storing all food, cooking items, feed, cosmetics and coolers properly stored when at campgrounds or in the backcountry.

al.d: All units except the Turkey Creek Unit allow hunting. In hunting areas, hunting is not allowed within 500 feet of trails. Wear orange if entering a hunting area.

al.d: The interior of the Oakland Main House is ONLY open to the public on Saturdays and Sundays from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. All tours of the house are self-guided and occupancy within the building is limited. Please plan accordingly.

al.t: Park Operating Hours
al.d: Operating hours are 9:00 am to 3:30 pm Wednesday through Sunday until further notice.

al.t: Weather Advisory and Storm Warnings
al.d: The park may have delayed openings or closures in the event of severe weather. Travel may not be recommended during these times. Please check local weather forecasts. We appreciate your understanding.

al.t: Route 7 from Sawmill, AZ is NOT recommended
al.d: Entering the park from the east at Sawmill, AZ on Route 7 is not recommended. Part of this route is UNPAVED and UNMAINTAINED. Please stay on paved roads, such as Indian Route 64 from Tsaile, AZ and Highway 191/Route 7 from Chinle, AZ.

al.t: Mineral Bottom and White Rim Road Remain Muddy in Parts, Not Recommended
al.d: The Mineral Bottom Road switchbacks and west side of the White Rim Road still have slippery and muddy sections due to recent rains. Travel is not recommended until the roads fully dry out.

al.t: Closure of Billy Mitchell Airport for Repaving Project
al.d: The Billy Mitchell Airport (HSE) is closed to accommodate a runway pavement rehabilitation project. The project will provide full resurfacing of paved areas, new reflective paint, and new tie-downs and anchors, improving visitor safety and enhancing the overall visitor experience.

al.t: Project Safety Closure in Place Near Southernmost Groin in Buxton
al.d: Public access is closed for 300 feet north and south of a groin repair project site in Buxton, as well as the adjacent ocean area to the east. Surfers, swimmers, and all other recreationists should stay at least 300 feet from the southernmost groin area for safety purposes.

al.t: Passenger Ferry Dock Closed; Visitors Deboard via Beach Landing
al.d: The ferry dock servicing the Cape Lookout Lighthouse area is closed for repairs. Visitors will deboard the ferry in front of the lighthouse. To reach the boardwalk, visitors will need to walk 5–10 minutes on soft sand. Depending on the tide, visitors may also need to walk through water.

al.t: Voice Mailboxes Down

al.t: Items Worn or Used in Other Caves Not Allowed
al.d: A disease known as White-Nose Syndrome is killing bats in North America. To prevent it from spreading to our bats, do not wear shoes, clothing, or bring any gear into any cave at Carlsbad Caverns National Park that were in another cave.

al.t: Timed Entry Ticket Required to Enter Carlsbad Cavern
al.d: Reservations are highly recommended and can be purchased by clicking "more" or calling 877-444-6777. Reservations only select the entry time. Upon arrival at the visitor center, an entrance pass must be purchased.

al.t: Footwear in the Cavern
al.d: For safety, closed-toe shoes with good traction are recommended. Flip flops, sandals, and some walking shoes have little or no traction and increase the possibility of slips, trips, and falls. Watch your step and use the handrails when necessary.

al.d: Louisiana Circle is closed to vehicles and pedestrians due to slope instability. Navy Circle is open and also provides views of the Mississippi River.

al.t: Trail Conditions
al.d: Rain may cause trails to be slick and overgrown. Staff and Volunteer Trail Crews clear trails regularly. Visitors should use caution and report trail issues to viis_interpretation@nps.gov

al.d: A portion of the Echo Bay Trail in Kabetogama will be temporarily closed Nov. 6–22 during hunting season. al.t: Limited access to areas at Asan Beach.
al.d: Due to the impacts of Typhoon Sinlaku, areas of Asan Beach remain inaccessible. Visitors should use caution when walking to the beach area and stay out of damaged areas.

al.t: No Winter Maintenance on Battlefield Trail
al.d: The battlefield trail is open year round, but receives no winter maintenance. There may be ice or snow on the trail. Please use caution.

al.t: No Recreational Vehicle (RV) Parking
al.d: Our parking lot cannot accommodate RVs or trailers. Check out our FAQs page or follow the link for a map to a nearby lot for parking and trailers to detach. RVs should NOT pull into the parking lot.

al.d: Whiskeytown National Recreation Area, in conjunction with U.S. Wildland Fire Service personnel, plan to conduct prescribed fire near the eastern boundary of the park between Whiskeytown Lake and the Shasta Divide Ridge in western Shasta County. al.t: Don't Move a Mussel!
al.d: Hey Boaters, please clean, drain, and dry your vessel completely before setting out on Whiskeytown Lake. Thank you for doing your part to keep the Golden Mussel, an aquatic invasive species, out of the reservoir. Learn more about preventative measures.

al.t: Dunes Drive Safety Corridor
al.d: Dunes Drive is open. A safety corridor is in effect between mile marker 3 and 5.5 along Dunes Drive. Visitors may drive but not stop or exit their vehicle in this area.

al.t: Backcountry Camping Closed
al.d: Backcountry camping at the park is closed. There is no established opening date at this time.

al.t: Interdune Boardwalk Closed
al.d: Due to the active safety corridor, the Interdune Boardwalk is closed. Please visit the park visitor center to learn about other options during your visit.

al.t: Park Closures
al.d: From time to time the missile range that surrounds the park performs military testing that may require the closure of the park or Highway 70. Please plan your visit around upcoming military tests.

al.t: RV and Tractor Trailer Parking at the Visitor Center
al.d: There is limited space for parking for recreational vehicles and trailers in the parking lot directly in front (south) of the visitor center. RVs are asked to not park in the lot behind the visitor center. There is no parking space for tractor trailers.

al.t: Phone Lines Currently Down
al.d: The Whitman Mission NHS phone lines are currently down. If you need to contact us, please email whmi_interpretation. For field trip scheduling, please email whmi_education@nps.gov

parks.n: William Howard Taft National Historic Site

al.t: Weekend Guided Tours Availability
al.d: Please visit the Guided Tours of the Taft Family Home page to review the tour times available for visitors on weekend day visits.

al.t: America the Beautiful Pass not Issued at Wilson's Creek
al.d: Wilson's Creek National Battlefield is a fee free site. No pass or charge is required to visit. Due to being a fee free site, America the Beautiful Passes are no longer issued. To learn about different pass types and where you can obtain them, including new digital passes, please visit the provided

al.t: Navigation Warning
al.d: Some navigation systems on devices misdirect visitors driving to Wilson’s Creek National Battlefield. Please note that the entrance to the park is at the visitor center located near the Southeast intersection of Hwy ZZ and FR 182.

al.t: Natural Entrance Tour Route Closes For Season October 1, 2026
al.d: The Natural Entrance Tour Route will be closed for the season beginning October 1st, 2026. The Garden of Eden, Fairgrounds, and Accessibility Tour Routes remain available. This annual closure will last through the winter season.

al.t: Centennial Trailhead Parking
al.d: Reminder: Overnight parking without a camping permit is prohibited. Permits are not issued specifically for parking. Shuttles are available in the Black Hills for through hikers on the Centennial Trail.

al.t: Wind Cave moves to cashless fee collection
al.d: Payments for cave tours, campground fees, as well as Interagency Passes at Wind Cave National Park, will be by credit/ debit cards or digital payments only. Cash and check payments will no longer be accepted.

al.t: Elevator is Out-of-Service
al.d: The elevator at the Visitor Center is currently out-of-service, due to regularly scheduled maintenance. We apologize for the inconvenience and encourage visitors to visit the virtual tours available on our website.

al.t: Wupatki VC Phone Outages
al.d: The main phone line for the visitor center experiences occasional outages. Please email FLAG_Information@nps.gov if you have trouble getting through on the main number.

al.t: Most Park Roads Closed to All Vehicles
al.d: Most roads are closed to prepare for commercially-guided snowcoach and snowmobile travel during the winter season, which will begin December 15 (weather depending). The road between the North and Northeast entrances is the only road open year-round to regular vehicles.

al.t: Biscuit Basin Closed Due to Hydrothermal Explosion
al.d: The parking lot, boardwalk, and Firehole River at Biscuit Basin, located north of Old Faithful, is closed to all travel until further notice due to the possibility of another event at the site of a hydrothermal explosion that occurred July 23, 2024.

al.t: Traffic Delays - Gardner River High Bridge
al.d: Expect a single lane of traffic with up to 15-minute delays, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, from April 1 through November 24, 2026. Oversized/overweight vehicles (8'6"+ wide, 75'+ long, 80,000 lbs+ gross vehicle weight) will not be able to cross the bridge during this time.

al.t: Rehabilitation of Colonial Parkway continues with additional Parkway closures
al.d: Beginning Tuesday, April 9, 2024, construction will close the Colonial Parkway to all travel in either direction between Yorktown and VA Route 199. Follow all detour signs. See additional closure information in the link below.

al.t: Tioga Road and Glacier Point Road are temporarily closed
al.d: Tioga Road (continuation of Highway 120 through the park) and Glacier Point Road are temporarily closed due to a forecast of snow. Call 209/372-0200 (then 1, 1) to check road conditions in the park.

al.t: No overnight parking on Tioga & Glacier Point Roads
al.d: Overnight parking is not allowed on Tioga Road and Glacier Point Road, including all parking lots reachable from these roads.

al.t: Sheep Hunting Closure

al.t: Watchman Trail closed
al.d: The Watchman Trail is closed pending repairs.

al.t: Large vehicle restrictions on Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway
al.d: Vehicles that exceed length, width, height, or weight limits cannot travel between Canyon Junction and the park's East Entrance. See the current limits on the page linked below.

al.t: Toxic cyanobacteria in rivers, streams, and pools
al.d: Do not submerge your head in or drink instream water in Zion National Park.

al.t: Angels Landing Pilot Permit Program
al.d: All hikers need a permit to hike Angels Landing. Learn why you need a permit and how to get one using the link below.

al.t: Please park legally and responsibly
al.d: Zion has limited parking. Once parking spaces in Zion are full, visitors should park in Springdale. Please park only in designated spaces. Vehicles parked outside of designated spaces are subject to citation and towing.
